skill.name: keyword-research
skill.description: Researches SEO and GEO keywords from seed topics, connected metrics, and user-provided data. It prioritizes volume, difficulty, intent, topic clusters, and content opportunities.
skill.summary: Builds prioritized keyword briefs with intent scoring and topic clusters.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are Markdown examples, metadata URLs, formulas, or relative documentation links and are false positives. Three helper-command findings are confirmed because the skill tells agents to run local Python connectors, and semantic review found third-party query disclosure plus an unsanitized save-path placeholder. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Optional helper commands can run local Python connector scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running each helper and show the exact command, input, service, and expected output.

remediation.issue: Connector workflows may disclose keywords or topics to third-party services.
remediation.suggestion: Add a consent note before Autocomplete, Firecrawl, pageviews, SEO tool, or Search Console calls that states what data is sent.

remediation.issue: The research save path uses a raw topic placeholder.
remediation.suggestion: Require slugifying the topic to letters, numbers, and hyphens before writing under memory/research/keyword-research/.

content.user_title: Research SEO Keywords and Topic Clusters
content.value_statement: Keyword planning is slow when volume, difficulty, intent, and clusters live in separate places. This skill turns seed topics and metrics into prioritized SEO and GEO keyword briefs.
actual_capabilities: Runs an eight-phase workflow from scope through delivery.
Expands seed terms into modifiers, long-tail variations, and topic ideas.
Classifies keywords by intent, funnel stage, content type, and CTA fit.
Scores opportunities using volume, difficulty, intent value, and optional impact confidence.
Groups keywords into pillar pages, cluster pages, and content calendar recommendations.
Labels metrics as Measured, User-provided, Estimated, or N/A.
limitations: Live volume and difficulty require connected SEO tools or user-provided exports.
Optional helper scripts may contact external services and need user approval.
Competitor-relative content gaps belong in a separate content-gap workflow.
Estimated metrics should be validated before budget or staffing decisions.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Content Program
use_cases.description: Turn a product, service, or topic into prioritized keywords, clusters, and first-month content ideas.

use_cases.title: Prioritize SEO Opportunities
use_cases.description: Compare keywords by volume, difficulty, intent, and business relevance before assigning writing work.

use_cases.title: Build GEO-Friendly Topic Coverage
use_cases.description: Find question, definition, comparison, and how-to queries that can support AI answer visibility.

prompt_templates.title: Start Keyword Research
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with a seed topic.
prompt_templates.prompt: Research keywords for [topic] in [market]. Use estimated metrics if no tool data is available, and label every estimate clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Map Search Intent
prompt_templates.prompt: Classify these keywords by intent, funnel stage, content format, and CTA. Highlight mixed-intent terms and explain the dominant intent.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize A Content Sprint
prompt_templates.prompt: Score these keyword ideas by volume, difficulty, intent value, business relevance, and confidence. Return quick wins, growth terms, and GEO opportunities.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Cluster Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a content hub.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a pillar and cluster plan for [topic]. Include primary keywords, secondary pages, internal links, publishing order, and measurement checkpoints.

output_examples.input: Research keywords for project management software for small businesses.
output: Top quick wins include small-team and spreadsheet-alternative terms with commercial intent.
The main pillar targets project management fundamentals, with clusters for collaboration and planning.
The first content sprint prioritizes low-difficulty commercial pages before broad head terms.

output_examples.input: Map intent for a list of SEO tool keywords.
output: Pricing and comparison terms map to commercial or transactional intent.
How-to and definition terms map to informational intent and GEO-friendly formats.
Brand and login terms are navigational and should not be treated as acquisition pages.

output_examples.input: Create a topic cluster plan for local accounting services.
output: The pillar page should cover the core service and target the highest business relevance term.
Cluster pages should cover local modifiers, pricing questions, tax deadlines, and industry-specific services.
Measurement should review indexing after two weeks and ranking trend after three months.

best_practices: Provide the target market, language, audience, and business goal before requesting keyword scoring.
Mark every metric source as measured, user-provided, estimated, or unavailable.
Use Search Console or SEO tool exports when decisions depend on exact volume or difficulty.
anti_patterns: Do not present estimated metrics as measured data.
Do not target high-volume terms without checking intent and ranking difficulty.
Do not create thin cluster pages when one stronger pillar section would answer the query.

faq.question: Does this skill fetch live keyword volume by itself?
faq.answer: No. It needs connected SEO tools, Search Console data, or user-provided exports for measured volume and difficulty.

faq.question: Can it work without SEO tools?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use seed terms, user knowledge, and clearly labeled estimates, but measured metrics will be unavailable.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a prioritized keyword brief with quick wins, growth terms, GEO opportunities, topic clusters, and next steps.

faq.question: How does it handle search intent?
faq.answer: It maps terms to informational, navigational, commercial, or transactional intent, then links them to content formats.

faq.question: Is this for competitor gap analysis?
faq.answer: No. It can consider competitor context, but competitor-relative coverage gaps need a content-gap analysis workflow.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, and Claude Code use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report metadata lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code compatible hosts.
